correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) give the three conditional expectations. Averaging them yields \(\mathbb E[y]=\mathbb E[z]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[x^2]=c\mathbb E[x]\), hence the exact variance parabola. Its endpoint rigidity follows because constant \(x\) on invariant support forces \(y=z=0\) and then \(x(x-c)=0\). The nonlinear forcing residual is exactly \(\dot z\), so conditional orthogonality gives the variance defect and covariance identity. Zero vertical speed on compact invariant support forces constant \(z\), then bounded completeness forces \(z=y=0\) and finally equilibrium support. The packaged checker independently verifies the algebra and sharp constants.

value.rationale: The Genesio flow is a canonical one-quadratic-nonlinearity jerk system whose literature centers on its two equilibria, Hopf/period-doubling routes, and chaotic attractor. The accepted theorem ties those equilibrium points directly to every compact stationary statistic: the barycenter is forced onto their connecting segment, and the x-variance is exactly the fixed-point chord product \(m(c-m)\), giving a sharp parameter-only envelope. The companion heightwise regression resolves the quadratic vertical forcing on each z-fiber and converts its unexplained component into exact mean-square vertical speed. These provide nontrivial, exact consistency diagnostics for periodic or chaotic invariant-state computations and are stronger than previously published scalar recurrence balances.
